_readme: THE COPILOT CAGE, AS DATA. Claude Code is caged by a settings file that
names the denied tools. GitHub Copilot CLI has no such file - it takes
the cage on the COMMAND LINE, so the cage here is a list of arguments
RUNME passes at launch.
VERIFIED AGAINST A LIVE CLI on 2026-07-30 (Copilot CLI 1.0.76) by asking
a real caged session to list the tools it could see. The previous
version of this file was written blind and was WRONG in three ways;
each is recorded here because the wrong shape reads exactly like the
right one:
1. --deny-tool DOES NOT HIDE A TOOL. It only decides whether a call
needs approval, and its patterns accept four kinds only - shell(),
write(), url() and <mcp-server>(). Names like view, read, search,
edit and str_replace are not kinds at all: they were accepted in
silence and did nothing. A probe run with the old deny_args still
saw powershell, view, create, edit, grep, glob, web_fetch, task and
sql. The cage was decoration.
2. --excluded-tools IS the analogue of Claude's bare-name deny: it
removes the tool from the model's context entirely. That is what
exclude_args below does, and the same probe then saw the se lane
and NOTHING else.
3. THE SERVER WAS NOT EVEN LOADING. Copilot does not read a project's
.copilot/mcp-config.json by itself - it reads ~/.copilot/mcp-config.json.
The workspace file has to be handed over with --additional-mcp-config,
which is what mcp_args does. Without it the agent had no se tools
at all, only its native ones - the exact inverse of the design.
THE BLACKLIST IS EXPLICIT, by the same owner ruling that shapes the
Claude cage: a tool Copilot ADDS IN A FUTURE VERSION is not blocked
automatically. Blocking it is a deliberate edit to exclude_args.
HOW TO RE-CHECK after a CLI update, in one command, from workspace/:

copilot -p "List the EXACT names of every tool you can currently see, one per line, nothing else." -s --additional-mcp-config "@.copilot/mcp-config.json" --disable-builtin-mcps --no-custom-instructions --excluded-tools <the list below>
Anything in that output which is not an se_ tool is a hole in the cage.
CONTRACT RULE 1 IS WHAT THIS ENFORCES: everything the agent does runs
through the se lane. If these flags do not hold, the cage is ADVISORY
on this host - the agent is asked rather than prevented.
_mcp_args: The se server, handed over explicitly. --disable-builtin-mcps drops
github-mcp-server, whose 17 tools are a second uncaged lane (the Claude
cage never had it). Without it the agent can read any repo on the host
_exclude_args: THE CAGE PROPER - these names vanish from the model's context.
Grouped as they map onto the Claude deny list.
task is excluded where Claude keeps it. Claude's subagents inherit the
parent's deny list, so they are caged too; a Copilot subagent is a
SEPARATE session that does not inherit --excluded-tools, so leaving it
would hand the agent an uncaged twin - the one hole big enough to walk
the whole cage through. Restore it only alongside a verified way to
_allow_args: The se lane is pre-approved, so the walk is not a wall of prompts -
this is Copilot's `mcp__se__*` allow. `se` is the server name as it is
written in .copilot/mcp-config.json; change one and change the other.
NOT --allow-all-tools: that would pre-approve anything a future CLI
adds, which is the opposite of an explicit list.
_deny_args: DEFENCE IN DEPTH, not the cage. Every kind here is a real one, so if a
shell or a write ever reaches the agent by another road, it still stops
to ask. These are the only four kinds --deny-tool understands.
